notes: 2026-02-15 - Intro call (Maya/Liam). Client: Orbit runs market data enrichment + conversational support for traders. High sensitivity to inference tail latency during spikes.

2026-02-18 - Perf workshop (ff_2026-02-18_orbit_prod-review). Ran initial Dedicated baseline on a1-gpu-reserve: synthetic qps 150 RPS at 256-token average. Observed p50 ~28ms (server token), p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms (non-streaming completion times).

Key ask from Orbit: guaranteed p95 < 200ms and p99 < 500ms for non-streaming completion under reserved capacity for typical peak of 200 RPS. Streaming requirement: client-side first-token p50 < 40ms, p95 < 250ms.

Redwood measurement alignment notes: Redwood backend reports server-side delta (request accept -> last token emitted). Client SDK measures end-to-end (client send -> receive last token) which adds network + SDK processing. We proposed mapping: SLA to be defined on server-side processing with client-side deltas tracked as advisory metric. Orbit pushed back — needs client-side guarantees for trading UX.

POC telemetry plan: 1) enable per-request token timing, 2) collect server and client traces for matched request ids, 3) baseline with continuous batching (max batch 8) and without batching. Plan to compare streaming vs non-streaming modes over a 72-hour window including synthetic spike (2x nominal load).

Latency definitions agreed in-workshop (draft): p50/p95/p99 for two categories — 'completion latency' (non-streaming, measured server-side from accept->final token) and 'first-token latency' (streaming, measured server-side from accept->first-token). Client-side timing will be measured by Orbit's SDK and logged; discrepancies must remain <= 40ms median under normal network conditions.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning: Orbit asks for capacity plan for 3x peak headroom. Based on model (orca-m-medium quantized), observed throughput per GPU ~4800 tokens/sec steady with batching. For 200 RPS @ 256 tokens/request => ~51k tokens/sec steady peak. Recommendation: 12 GPUs reserved (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) with autoscale buffer to handle spikes. Redwood to provide explicit throughput guarantees in SLA with burn-rate accounting for streaming token bursts.

SLA negotiation points: credit calculation tied to rolling 1-hour window breaches of p99 completion > agreed threshold, exclusion for external network outages, ability to fall back to a lower-capacity cheaper model with prior notice, and retention period for traces 90 days for audit. Legal requested example credit table; AE committed to provide draft by 2026-03-12.

Measurement alignment technical detail: Need common clock baseline. Action: instrument synchronized NTP-based timestamps in SDK and server; include request_id header for trace stitching. Also add a 'client_observed_latency' field in server logs when present.
